subject: Aligning March top-up to annual renewal — proposal and timeline
body:
From: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@orchidhealth.com>
Subject: Mid-cycle increase — March usage surge and billing alignment

Hi Naomi,

We are seeing a faster-than-expected onboarding cadence at Orchid and likely need a 35% increase in token capacity starting March 15 for ~2 months while a new cohort ramps. Our procurement team prefers to simply top up now and have that usage aligned or credited toward our anniversary renewal on May 12 if possible.

Can Redwood provide guidance on:
- An interim pricing model for a short-term capacity increase (Mar 15–May 12)
- Whether that top-up can be credited/annualized at renewal (co-term) and how credits would be calculated
- Any required paperwork or PO needed to lock in the temporary capacity

I've attached a quick usage forecast and the internal ask.

Thanks,
Emma
[Attachment: Orchid_Growth_Request.xlsx (XLSX)]

---
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 11:00:00 -0700
To: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle increase — March usage surge and billing alignment

Hi Emma — thanks for the details and the forecast. Quick notes up front: we can do a short-term top-up with a simple PO, and we have two common approaches people choose from depending on whether you want billing simplicity now vs. accounting alignment at renewal. I'll outline both and flag ask items.

Option A — Short-term top-up (fastest):
- Start date: Mar 15
- Billed pro-rata for the 2-month window at your current committed unit price
- No automatic credit at renewal (clean accounting for this quarter)
- Minimal paperwork: a PO referencing a one-time top-up invoice

Option B — Top-up convertible to renewal (co-term credit):
- Start date: Mar 15
- Billed pro-rata now at 85% of the committed price (introductory top-up discount)
- If you renew/expand on May 12, the spent top-up amount converts to a pre-payment and is applied against the new annual commitment (effectively annualizing the top-up)
- Requires a short amendment/terms addendum so finance can recognize as credit toward renewal

To proceed I need: preferred option, PO number (if Option A) or internal renewal intent note (if Option B), and any compliance docs you require. Ben — looping you for numbers and recommended credit calculation. Monica — adding you to ensure CS handover timing is covered.

Best,
Naomi

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@orchidhealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle increase — March usage surge and billing alignment

Emma / team — pricing clarity below. For the 35% uplift for Mar15–May12 we can do:

- Standard pro-rata invoice (Option A): at your current commit rate = $0.0009 per token equivalent; estimated invoice ~$28k for the period (see attached calc).
- Convertible top-up (Option B): bill at 85% of commit rate (effective $0.000765/token) and if you commit to a 12-month renewal by May 12, we convert the invoice dollars to credit that counts toward tiering. If you don't renew, the invoice remains as paid usage.

Credit math (Option B): the paid top-up dollars = credit applied 1:1 to the first year's invoice, then standard tier bands apply. Example: $24k top-up becomes $24k prepayment against the renewal. If renewal tier pushes you into a discount band, the prepayment still reduces net invoice dollars.

We can also offer a one-time 5% onboarding credit if you sign the renewal within 30 days post top-up. That helps offset the short-term spike.

Attachment: "RW-topup-calculation-March2027.xlsx" (summary included in Orchid_Growth_Request.xlsx)

---
From: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 08:30:00 -0700
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@orchidhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle increase — March usage surge and billing alignment

Thanks Naomi and Ben — Option B (convertible top-up) sounds closest to what procurement needs, but two constraints:
1) Our legal team needs the amendment to cap the potential committed increase so it doesn't automatically expand our minimum annual commitment. In other words, the top-up must be clearly labeled as a prepayment/credit only, not a binding increase to our MRR.
2) We need paperwork that won't delay the Mar 15 start by more than 48 hours — procurement has a short approval window.

Can Redwood draft the amendment language that explicitly states the top-up converts to a credit at renewal only if Orchid signs a renewal amendment, otherwise it remains paid usage? Also need the PO format for the top-up invoice.

Emma

---
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 15:20:00 -0700
To: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@orchidhealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle increase — March usage surge and billing alignment

Emma — understood on the legal cap. Proposed operational compromise to keep Mar 15 start and address procurement/legal concerns:

- We will issue a one-off invoice for the top-up (PO accepted) dated Mar 15 billed at the convertible rate (85% of commit).
- Internal amendment (non-binding for minimum commitment) will be titled "Top-up Credit Addendum" and will state: 1) Top-up is a paid prepayment; 2) It may be applied to a future renewal only if Orchid elects to execute a renewal amendment within the specified window; 3) It will not raise the minimum annual commitment absent explicit agreement.
- Add a 30-day renewal incentive (5% credit on net new commit) as Ben suggested.
- Legal/Procurement draft will be ready for signature within 24 hours; Naomi/Ben — can Legal expedite redline and return to Emma's team?

If this works for Orchid we can start provisioning on Mar 15. Monica — can your onboarding plan cover an accelerated burst?

Thanks,
Vivek

---
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 16:43:00 -0700
To: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@orchidhealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle increase — March usage surge and billing alignment

Emma / Liam — confirming next steps so we can meet your Mar 15 window: 
1) We will provision additional capacity on Mar 15 once we receive a PO for the convertible top-up. Please include PO number and billing contact.
2) Legal will send the Top-up Credit Addendum draft by COB tomorrow (Mar 12) and will explicitly include the language you requested capping the minimum commitment.
3) Ben will issue the provisional invoice at the convertible rate; payment will clear as a prepayment credit if Orchid signs renewal amendment by May 12.
4) Monica will schedule a short onboarding burst plan (Mar 15–Mar 22) and confirm operational readiness.

Document & links: 
- Draft will reference HubSpot deal ORC-2027-1542 and DocuSign envelope (https://redwood.app/docusign/abc123).
- Attach: RW-proposal-q2-2027.pdf (formal pricing sheet) will follow in separate email.

Emma — if you can reply with "Option B — PO <number> incoming" or with the PO attached, we will treat that as authorization to proceed.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
